title: Experiment: the change-stream server, deterministic under injection and live in production
summary: Nine tests against the shipping service with the watcher and timers injected, so failure, heartbeat, disconnect and cleanup are decided rather than waited for. Measured: nothing starts until the first subscription (no watcher, no timer); a heartbeat is a NAMED event carrying `{ok:true}`; two subscribers both receive a change hint and a late subscriber receives no replay; one subscriber leaving clears its own timer and leaves the shared watcher running for the other; the last one leaving closes it; a watcher `error` broadcasts a named `failure` event with the reason AND closes every stream, leaving no timer; a subscriber whose send throws is dropped without affecting the rest; and `close()` ends every stream, releases the watcher and refuses further subscriptions. IN PRODUCTION, against a real build serving a temporary content root, an event-stream client read `/events` incrementally and observed `event: heartbeat` with `data: {"ok":true}`, then `event: change` after a real file write, with no `id:` field anywhere.

facts.contentRoot: a disposable copy; the project's own content was not touched

omissions.reason: A watcher error was injected, not provoked. A real one needs the OS to run out of watch descriptors or a directory to vanish under the process, neither of which can be asked for on demand — which is exactly why the collaborator is injectable.
This is the SERVER half. Whether a browser's EventSource fires a listener for these frames, and what a watchdog does when they stop, is TSK-0017's and ACC-0029/ACC-0030 remain not-evaluated.
The production stream was read for seconds, not hours. Whether an idle connection survives a long period, and whether subscriber cleanup holds under many connect/disconnect cycles, was not exercised.

notes: ⚠️ THE INJECTION IS WHAT MAKES THE FAILURE PATH TESTABLE AT ALL. `ENOSPC: watchers exhausted` is not something a test can cause; without an injectable watcher the most important behaviour in this component — that a dead watcher tells every page rather than only the log — would have been asserted by reading the code. ⚠️ THE PRODUCTION CHECK READS THE STREAM INCREMENTALLY AND STOPS. An event stream never finishes, so `await res.text()` would hang until the timeout and report a working stream as a failure. The reader is released as soon as both frames have been seen. ⚠️ FALSIFIED THREE WAYS, each failing only its own assertion: replacing the named heartbeat with a comment keepalive fails the production check; logging a watcher failure instead of broadcasting it fails the failure test; tearing the watcher down on the first disconnect fails the shared-watcher test.
